segments.text: [MUSIC PLAYING]
SPEAKER: Are you tired of making your users
download the same data every time they launch your app,
but don't want to add the complexity of databases
or document storage?
If so, and you are programming for mobile or desktop,
try using path_provider to access the device's file
system.
To start, call the get Application Documents Directory
method provided by path_provider.
This method returns a directory object that points
to the location on your user's device
that the operating system has allocated for your app.
Here you can create files to store
large blobs of binary data, raw JSON that
was expensive to load from the server,
or well, anything you can imagine.
And what if you have different data,
like manifest files or other supporting
documents from your server?
For that, call get Application Support Directory.
And what if you just need a temporary folder
for data that doesn't need to outlive the current session?
Then call get Temporary Directory.
In any of these scenarios, you have a place
to cache free form data as needed
to ensure that your app is as performant as possible.
Just don't forget to clean up after yourself.
Deleting old unwanted files prevents
wasting your user storage.
So if the hassle of SQLite or document storage isn't for you,
reach for path_provider to easily cache expensive data.
For more info on path_provider and all the other packages,
head to pub.dev.
